conclusion: A longer client-only diagnostic of the joint 7+1 worker allocation and ingress-isolation treatment. All six outcomes and actual generated work are retained; this report establishes no reliability fix, unique causal mechanism, failure-rate ranking or server performance improvement.
scope: Longer client-only pressure-sustainability diagnostic, never server performance acceptance or proof of a reliability fix. The new workload changes only offer duration from4seconds to16seconds relative to the recorded B/D argument recipes. B retains8shared application workers; D retains7application workers plus1dedicated endpoint ingress worker, with the same CPUs8-15 total allowance and ready-gate placement. The same frozen737server, client binaries, message rates,1024readers, body verification, pacing, requested4MiB UDP buffer and1second drain are retained. All six fixed rotated cases run through ordinary failures. Three repetitions per arm do not establish a failure rate, winner or unique causal mechanism. Review actual generated work and lag before interpreting any apparent benefit. Observer-instrumented timing/CPU/RSS are diagnostic measurements.
stopping_rule: Run all six fixed cases. Ordinary workload failures do not stop the series; infrastructure errors abort with a preserved partial summary.
generation_semantics: Generated is counted after successful local send completion, not server receipt. Lag is sampled before the send against its schedule; last_submit_ms is after send completion. Histogram p50/p99 are bucket upper bounds; max_ms is exact for observed samples. A 4-second cutoff can leave a few planned updates ungenerated; every actual count is reported without an invented completeness threshold.
limits: D jointly reallocates one of eight application workers to a dedicated endpoint runtime and isolates that runtime on CPU 8. It does not isolate runtime placement from application-pool size; a 7-worker shared-runtime control was not run.

D and B share the same total runtime-worker/core budget on CPUs 8-15. Both also have a coordinator thread allowed on CPUs 8-15. This is not an additional ninth runtime worker or eight-plus-one CPU treatment.
Connection/application futures still use the application runtime. Thread counters do not directly attribute individual migrating futures or prove exact endpoint wake delay.

One shared UDP socket, requested 4 MiB receive buffer, certificate pin, traffic, pacing and verification are unchanged. Sampled queue accounting is kernel socket memory accounting, not application payload or complete kernel memory.

UDP peaks and cumulative drops are observed at actual sample times; sub-sample peaks or bursts can be missed. The socket lifetime window includes setup/cleanup; ready-to-measured drop deltas are reported separately.
CPU ticks are quantized and per-thread reads are sequential. OS schedstat wait is runnable-thread wait, not Tokio future wait; disabled schedstats cannot establish absence of starvation.
Requested 4 ms UDP and 40 ms CPU cadence are targets; actual gaps and collector costs are retained. Observer-instrumented CPU/RSS/timing is not an ordinary server benchmark.
Cleanup receipts establish normal close counts and zero retained relay accounting; successful process exit bounds thread lifetime. They are not a per-allocation or kernel-object leak proof.

D intentionally retains the ingress guard through the done gate; it signals and joins the ingress thread after that gate is continued. Teardown is supported by source lifetime and successful process exit, without a separate post-join event.
Historical individual source-file references describe archived source. Canonical B/C/D archives were verified; the shared build tree is currently restored to C while its target cache can contain D.

This 16-second workload is distinct from the earlier 4-second workload. The only recipe change is offer duration; the drain remains 1 second. Compare actual generated counts and lag, not duration-scaled expectations alone.
A failed case without a measured gate has unknown partial generation and measured-phase CPU; its sampled lifetime pressure is retained without pretending it offered the full plan.

The dedicated ingress still has one computational worker. Gate-average CPU includes the drain and does not exclude shorter saturation near one core or prove spare ingress capacity. D3 queue pressure is retained even when no UDP drops are observed.

Descriptive summaries retain case labels, sample counts and measured-gate availability. Lifetime UDP maxima from early failures span shorter windows and are not equivalent exposure or performance rankings.
